issues.description: The template declares the framebuffer base symbol display_start in pixel.asm (section .bss) but the solution file removes that declaration while still referencing display_start in code. This inconsistency (symbol declared in the template but not defined in the solution while being used) will confuse students and may cause assembly/link errors or unclear expectations about where the framebuffer resides.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the framebuffer base symbol display_start consistent across artifacts. Restore the display_start declaration (e.g. 'display_start RESB 8294400' in the .bss section) in the solution file, or explicitly document and implement the new location/definition (e.g. allocate it on the stack and update all references). Ensure the template, problem statement and solution reference the same symbol definition so students have a clear, buildable baseline.
